requirements.requirement: The system must define a Pydantic request model that accepts a list of provider identifiers (NPIs or internal IDs) as a required field.
The system must enforce that the provider identifier list contains at least two unique providers.
The system must reject requests where provider identifiers are duplicated within the input list.
The system must define a Pydantic response model that returns a ranked list of providers ordered by comparison score.
The system must include an overall normalized score for each provider in the response schema.
The system must include a measure-level breakdown for each provider consistent with existing evaluation output structure.
The system must include strengths for each provider as a structured list derived from explanation outputs.
The system must include weaknesses for each provider as a structured list derived from explanation outputs.
The system must ensure the response schema is compatible with existing provider evaluation response formats from EVAL-SCORE-PROV.
The system must ensure the response schema is compatible with explanation outputs from EVAL-EXPLAIN.
The system must include a rank field for each provider indicating its position in the comparison result.
The system must define explicit field types and validation rules in Pydantic models for all request and response attributes.
The system must raise a validation error if fewer than two provider identifiers are provided in the request.
The system must raise a validation error if any provider identifier is null, empty, or improperly formatted.
The system must structure the response so it can be directly consumed by downstream API/tool_router without transformation.
The system must include a comparison metadata section in the response indicating total providers compared and timestamp of generation.
The system must ensure deterministic field naming and ordering in the schema to support consistent LLM consumption.
The system must allow optional inclusion of raw measure scores alongside normalized scores in the response schema.
